key_insight: Activated TIG (A-TIG) cuts welding electricity use by about 40% versus conventional TIG, but it can increase photochemical ozone creation impacts because of methanol-based flux emissions and upstream production.
engineering_relevance: For penetration-matched 304L stainless-steel welds, A-TIG offers a lower-energy path with environmental trade-offs, making flux design and parameter tuning critical for sustainable welding.
method: Cradle-to-gate LCA in SimaPro 9.2 with Ecoinvent 3 datasets
Compared conventional TIG vs. TiO2-methanol A-TIG for 100 mm bead-on-plate welds
Assessed midpoint impacts with EPD 2018 and endpoint impacts with ReCiPe 2016; ran one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis (30 scenarios)
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower acidification, eutrophication, and global warming impacts for A-TIG, nearly identical water scarcity, and a 68.1 percentage-point higher normalized POCP score, with the ranking unchanged across sensitivity tests.
watch_item: Results are cradle-to-gate model estimates for bead-on-plate welds, so they may not directly transfer to industrial joint geometries or real occupational exposure conditions.
paper_title: Life Cycle Assessment of Activated TIG Welding: Energy and Environmental Trade-offs in an Iranian Case Study with Sensitivity Analysis
